title: Hotpath attenuation rewrite and windowed KV prefetch to consolidate INT8/FP8 fast paths
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Redesigned quantized hotpath: merges dequant/requant stages, adds windowed KV prefetcher, and scheduling heuristics for continuous batching. Improves throughput for INT8/FP8 mixed workloads with minimal p95 latency impact. Backwards-compatible with existing quantized model profiles.
description:
Context & motivation: Several production workloads (ENG-1984) showed that the majority of per-token CPU/GPU overhead for quantized models comes from frequent small dequant/requant transitions and scattered KV cache misses when sequences have high prefix reuse. This PR consolidates the fast path by introducing a 'hotpath attenuator' that folds adjacent dequant/requant operations for INT8/FP8 fused kernels and pairs it with a windowed KV prefetcher that materializes likely KV ranges ahead of time for continuous-batching traffic. The goal is a measurable throughput improvement for mixed-precision models and steadier p95 latency under bursty arrival patterns.

What this change does (summary): - Adds a hotpath attenuation pass in the execution planner that detects foldable dequant/requant pairs and rewrites them into a single composite op with an optimized kernel hook. The composite op carries per-channel scale LUT references so we avoid repeated host-side scale transforms. - Implements windowed KV prefetcher in the scheduler: per-request predictions (small LRU-weighted histogram) select a KV window to prefetch into the local KV cache, reducing remote reads for repeated prefixes. The prefetcher is tunable per model via config flags (window_size, prefetch_threshold). - Adjusts continuous-batching heuristics: the batcher will now favor requests with high KV-affinity to improve kernel utilization while keeping latency SLOs via an adaptive deadline parameter. - Low-level kernel changes: new fused kernel path for INT8->accum->FP8 output that uses vectorized per-channel requant LUTs and a microkernel register tiling to reduce memory pressure. - Safety & compatibility: when foldability is ambiguous, we fall back to the original separate ops. Deprecated runtime flags are preserved, and model version pinning keeps behavior stable for previously pinned model configs.

Benchmark highlights (internal lab): - GPT-style 1B test: sustained throughput +22% (tokens/sec) when using INT8 fast path consolidated vs baseline dequant/requant pipeline. p50 latency: +1ms, p95: +2.8ms (within SLO for most customers). - Mixed precision FP8/INT8 workload: throughput +18% averaged across sequence lengths [64,512]. - KV-heavy conversational trace replay: median remote KV miss reduced by 63% with window_size=32 and prefetch_threshold=0.6. - Microbenchmarks: fused kernel shows 1.6x reduction in per-token memory traffic on representative layers.

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: add hotpath attenuator pass to planner and unit tests for fold detection - 2b3c4d5: implement windowed KV prefetcher + scheduler integration and config flags - 3c4d5e6: fused INT8->FP8 requant kernel and microkernel optimizations + benchmarks + docs - 4d5e6f7: end-to-end integration tests, CI fixes, and perf test harness updates

Files changed (high level): - src/runtime/planner/hotpath_attenuator.cc/.h - src/runtime/scheduler/windowed_prefetcher.cc/.h - src/runtime/kernel/fused_quant_kernels.cc - src/runtime/kernel/pc_lut_requant_microkernel.S - src/runtime/batcher/continuous_batcher.cc - integration_tests/perf/quant_hotpath_replay.yaml - docs/ops/quant_hotpath.md - tools/perf/bench_scripts/kv_prefetch_runner.py - ci/flake/adjust_timeouts.yml

Testing & CI: - Unit tests: new fold detection unit tests and negative cases added. - Integration tests: replay harness with representative conv traces. - Bench CI: added a synthetic bench that runs on the benchmark-lab infra and posts summary numbers to the PR. - CI result here initially failed one flaky test (quant_hotpath_unit::fold_detect_negative) on 2026-02-20; root cause was an edge-case when scale LUT has near-zero channels — added a guard and re-ran. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (high-level, chronological): - Marco Diaz (reviewer): "Nice consolidation. Two asks: (1) ensure the prefetcher respects VPC/zone-affinity to avoid cross-region prefetch costs, (2) add a small fuzz test to catch false-positive fold decisions." - Priya (author): "Added zone-affinity check and a new fuzz harness under integration_tests/ (commit 2b3c4d5). The fuzz will run in bench CI jobs and is feature-guarded behind PERF_DEBUG flag." - Ellen Park (reviewer): "Kernel looks good; microkernel naming and ABI change needs a changelog entry because downstream on-prem packaging uses symbol checks." - Priya: "Added symbol compatibility wrapper and a docs note in ops changelog." - Jordan Liu (reviewer): "Observed p95 regressions on a low-memory GPU profile in the perf runner. Can we add a fallback to the old path for devices with <8GB available?" - Priya: "Added runtime check to avoid fused path on devices with <8GB memory; the build includes that guard and tests pass. See commit 3c4d5e6." - Marco Diaz: "Approving after the device guard and VPC-affinity check. Verified bench numbers on benchmark-lab (run 2026-02-23)." - Ellen Park: "Approved. Left a docs nit which was addressed by author." - Merge: squash/merge performed after approvals and green CI.

Compatibility & rollout plan: - Feature is behind a runtime flag: quant_hotpath.enabled (default true on hosted for now). - Canary rollout: enable for 10% of requests for two weeks, with auto-rollback if p95 regression >5ms or token-error-rate increases. - Dedicated/Private: flag defaults to off; customers can opt-in via console or config. - Metrics to watch: quant.hotpath.fold_rate, kv.prefetch.hit_rate, batcher.affinity_score, p50/p95 latency per model, and token error rate.

Follow-ups & future work: - Expand fold detection to include weight-dropout cases (ENG-2021 follow-up). - Tune prefetcher machine-learned predictor (currently a lightweight histogram); plan an offline experiment to replace with a small predictor if stable. - Explore packing fused kernels for multi-layer fusion in next sprint.
